topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapy approaches and mechanisms.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional therapeutic modalities that debulk tumors or disrupt cellular replication, along with their associated clinical limitations and toxicities.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic tumor vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain strategies that exploit cancer-specific biological defects, including hormone receptor dependence, cell cycle checkpoint alterations, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the identification of driver oncogenes, the design of small-molecule kinase inhibitors targeting ATP binding sites, and the mechanisms behind acquired drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates are directed against cell surface antigens to eliminate tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the role of the immune system in tumor surveillance and examine therapies that reactivate, redirect, or engineer T cells to destroy cancer cells.

topics.label: Systemic challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical challenges of tumor heterogeneity and resistance, historical improvements in patient survival, and the strategic and ethical considerations for future cancer management.
